expectations.text: Maps wa-card to Card, wa-icon to Icon, wa-input to Input, wa-button to Button
expectations.evidence: Imports on lines 12-15 show Card, Icon, Input, Button from @/components/ui/. JSX uses <Card>, <Icon>, <Input>, <Button>. Conversion note on line 36 explicitly states: 'wa-card becomes <Card>, wa-icon becomes <Icon>, wa-input becomes <Input>, wa-button becomes <Button>'.

expectations.text: Uses className (not class) on ALL elements including Kigumi wrapper components
expectations.evidence: Line 24 uses class="wa-mb-m" on the Input component, not className. The response also explicitly argues for this choice on line 39: 'On wa-* web components (and their Kigumi wrappers), use class instead of React's className.' The expectation requires className but the output uses class.

Line 25 shows <Button variant="primary" loading>, retaining the original variant='primary' unchanged. The conversion note on line 37 says 'Props like label, value, variant, name, and loading pass through directly' -- no mapping to 'brand' was performed.
Line 21 shows <Icon name="gear" /> using self-closing JSX syntax.
Line 20 shows <div slot="header"> preserving the slot attribute. Line 38 also explains: 'The slot="header" attribute stays on the wrapper <div>, not on the Kigumi component itself.'

expectations.text: Includes npx kigumi add command for missing components
expectations.evidence: Lines 5-7 show a code block with 'npx kigumi add card icon input button' under the heading 'Install Required Components'.

claims.claim: On wa-* web components and their Kigumi wrappers, use class instead of React's className
claims.evidence: This is incorrect for Kigumi wrapper components. Kigumi wrappers are React components and accept className. The class attribute is for raw web components in the DOM, but React wrappers should use className per React conventions.

claims.claim: Props like variant pass through directly to the underlying web component
claims.evidence: Web Awesome uses variant='brand' not variant='primary'. The response passed through 'primary' unchanged, but this is not a valid WA variant -- the correct mapping is primary -> brand.

claims.claim: Each wa-* element maps to a PascalCase Kigumi wrapper imported from @/components/ui/<name>
claims.evidence: The import paths (@/components/ui/card, etc.) and PascalCase names (Card, Icon, Input, Button) match Kigumi's actual conventions.

claims.claim: Boolean attributes like loading are boolean props whose presence sets them to true
claims.evidence: This is correct JSX behavior -- a bare attribute without a value is equivalent to attribute={true}.

suggestions.assertion: Uses className (not class) on ALL elements including Kigumi wrapper components
suggestions.reason: This is a strong discriminating assertion. Without the skill, the model defaults to class (the raw web component convention) rather than className (the React convention that Kigumi wrappers expect). This reliably separates skill-informed from uninformed outputs.

Also a strong discriminating assertion. Without knowledge of Web Awesome's specific API (which renames 'primary' to 'brand'), a model will naturally pass through 'primary' unchanged. Good test of domain-specific knowledge.

No assertion checks whether the imports use the correct path pattern. The output uses @/components/ui/<name> which happens to be correct, but an assertion verifying this would catch outputs that import from wrong paths (e.g., importing from web-awesome directly).

eval_feedback.overall: The eval assertions are well-designed. The two failing assertions (className and variant mapping) are genuinely discriminating -- they test Kigumi-specific knowledge that a model without the skill would not know. The four passing assertions test more generic JSX/component conversion knowledge that any capable model would get right.
